features.id: Moving the caret with `withCaretAt(..)` to a coordinate at the place where a line wraps puts the caret on the line of that coordinate, like dragging the mouse there. [0]

extraInfo:
`withCaretAt(point)` moves the caret to the gap nearest to a pixel coordinate. Your code calls it when it
            moves the caret itself, for example while your users drag a round handle on a touch screen. Where a line
            wraps, one position is both the end of the upper line and the start of the next line, so the caret has
            two places for it. `withCaretAt(..)` picks the place on the line of the coordinate, just as dragging the
            mouse does: aimed at the end of the upper line, `isCaretAtLineEnd()` is `true` and `caretBounds()` lies
            at the end of the upper line; aimed at the start of the next line, it is `false` and `caretBounds()` lies
            at the start of the next line.

            The content area of the component is 100 pixels wide, and the text is "HHHH HHHH". At a font size of 20,
            one word of four "H" letters is about 56 pixels wide and a space about 5 pixels, so the two words need
            about 117 pixels and `wrapLines(true)` puts the second word onto a second line. Position 5 is the gap
            behind the space, which ends the first line and starts the second one.

            If `withCaretAt(..)` chose the place by where the anchor lies instead, a handle which your users drag to
            the start of the second line would jump back to the end of the first line, away from their finger.

            In this scenario the anchor is at position 2, and the coordinate lies at the start of the second line, behind the anchor.

features.id: With `placement(UI.Placement.TOP)`, a caret in an empty paragraph lies in the middle of the empty line, like the centred lines around it.

extraInfo:
Two line breaks in a row, the "\n" characters, make an empty paragraph, which SwingTree paints as an
            empty line. The placement decides where in the content area a line is painted, and an empty line follows
            it like every other line. With `placement(UI.Placement.TOP)` every line is centred horizontally, so a
            caret in the empty paragraph lies in the horizontal middle of the content area, between the middles of
            the lines above and below it.

            The component is 400 pixels wide and has a padding of 10 pixels, so its content area reaches from x = 10
            to x = 390, and its middle is at x = 200. The text is "First", two line breaks and "Third". A line break
            counts as one character, so position 6 is the gap between the two line breaks. If SwingTree put the caret
            of an empty line at the left edge of the content area, it would hang at x = 10, far away from the centred
            words.

features.id: With `withTextSelection("body", selection)` and an obstacle across the full width of the content area, a click on the obstacle puts the caret on the nearest line of text.

extraInfo:
An obstacle is a shape which you pass to `obstacles(..)`. SwingTree paints no text on it, and when it
            covers the content area from its left edge to its right edge, SwingTree paints no line at its height and
            continues the text below it. A click puts the caret into the gap nearest to the mouse, on the nearest
            line of text. A click on the obstacle is a click between two lines of text, so the caret goes to the
            line which is nearer to the mouse.

            The component is 240 pixels wide and has a padding of 10 pixels. The obstacle covers the full width
            from y = 40 to y = 80. The text is "HHHHHHHHHH " in red and "NNNNNNNNNN" in green. At a font size of 20,
            an "H" and an "N" are about 14 pixels wide, so the red word fits on the first line, above the obstacle,
            and the green word goes onto the next line, below the obstacle. Your user clicks at y = 70, near the
            bottom of the obstacle, above the middle of the green word. The green line is nearer to that point
            than the red line, so the caret goes into the green word, between position 11, in front of its first
            "N", and position 21, behind its last "N".

            If SwingTree treated the height which it skips at the obstacle as an empty line of its own, the click
            would land on that empty line, and the caret would jump to the start of the paragraph, at position 0.

features.id: With `withTextSelection()` and no property, your users can select and copy the text which `text(t -> ..)` declares without a name.

extraInfo:
`withTextSelection()` takes no property, for a text which your users should be able to select and copy
            while your code never needs to know what they selected. SwingTree then keeps the selection inside the
            component. It makes the text selectable which the style declares with `text(t -> ..)`, without a name,
            in the content layer.

            The component paints "Hello " in red and "world" in blue. Your user presses the mouse button on the left
            edge of the "w", drags it to the right edge of the "d" and releases it there. Then the scenario copies
            the selection by calling `exportToClipboard` on the `TransferHandler` of the component, which is what the
            keyboard shortcut for copying calls, with a clipboard that only this scenario uses. If SwingTree made the
            wrong text selectable, or none, the clipboard would stay empty.

features.id: Moving the anchor with `withAnchorAt(..)` keeps the caret and the line on which it lies, also where a line wraps.

extraInfo:
`withAnchorAt(..)` moves the anchor of a selection to the position nearest to a pixel coordinate, for
            example where your code paints a handle which your users drag. The caret is the other end of the
            selection, and it stays exactly where it was: at the same position, and on the same one of the two
            lines where its position is both the end of one line and the start of the next.

            The content area of the component is 100 pixels wide, and the text is "HHHH HHHH". With
            `wrapLines(true)` the first word and the space behind it go onto the first line, and the second word
            onto the second line, so position 5 ends the first line and starts the second. Your code selects from
            position 2 to position 5, so the caret lies at the end of the first line. Then it moves the anchor to
            the middle of the third green letter, on the second line, which is position 7. The selection now reaches
            from 7 back to 5, but its caret still lies at the end of the first line. If `withAnchorAt(..)` worked out
            the place of the caret again, the caret would jump to the start of the second line, although your users
            moved only the anchor.
